artworks.title: Bacchus and Ariadne
artworks.description: On Naxos Ariadne turns as Bacchus leaps from his cheetah chariot — Theseus' sail already pale on the horizon, the crown of stars foreshadowed above her head.

artworks.title: Ariadne Abandoned by Theseus
artworks.description: Kauffmann isolates the Naxos morning: Ariadne alone on the shore, the thread-giver left after the labyrinth, Catullus' abandoned heroine restaged for neoclassicism.

artworks.title: Sleeping Ariadne
artworks.artist: Unknown (Roman copy after a Hellenistic original)
artworks.description: The Vatican's reclining marble freezes the abandoned princess asleep on Naxos — antiquity's most famous image of the island vigil before Bacchus arrives.

artworks.title: Bacchus, Venus and Ariadne
artworks.description: Tintoretto's Doge's Palace canvas: Bacchus rises from the sea with a ring while Venus crowns Ariadne — Naxos as apotheosis, not only abandonment.

music.title: Ariadne auf Naxos
music.description: Strauss and Hofmannsthal nest the abandoned princess inside a comedy of opera itself — Naxos as meta-theatre.

music.title: L'Arianna
music.description: Monteverdi's lost Mantuan opera survives in Ariadne's lament — the cry of the woman Theseus left on Naxos.

popCulture.title: Ariadne
popCulture.description: Theseus' left-behind guide becomes Dionysus' bride — Naxos as the island of abandonment and apotheosis.
